div.h2: How We Build Custom Odoo POS Modules for Textile Businesses
div.p: When Al-Ghazl Al-Arabi Trading Company needed a way to manage fabric cutting orders directly from their Point of Sale, we built a custom Odoo 18 module that handles the entire workflow. Here's the technical architecture behind ma_pos_cutting — now published on the Odoo Apps Store.

The module extends PosOrder and PosOrderline with custom cutting fields (dimensions, fabric type, urgency level). We use OWL v3 components with a dedicated CuttingOrderScreen that renders inside the POS UI. Backend models connect to stock.picking for real-time warehouse updates when cuts are completed.

Moving from Odoo 16 to 18/19 required migrating from the old pos.db access pattern to pos.models['product.product']. The deprecated t-att-* directives on OWL components caused silent failures. We fixed IndexedDB serialization errors by overriding _load_pos_data_fields in Python to exclude mail.thread fields.

Our POS Stock Real-Time module (ma_rs_pos_stock) syncs inventory across all POS sessions using reactive badge updates via pos-stock-refreshed custom events. Batch loading handles catalogs with 10,000+ products. A navbar refresh button gives cashiers manual control.

div.h2: Implementing ZATCA E-Invoicing Compliance in Odoo
div.p: Saudi Arabia's ZATCA Phase 2 requires cryptographic signing and real-time API submission. We built a dual-system architecture to handle this while keeping POS operations on Odoo.sh for reliability.

Odoo.sh handles POS operations (uptime guaranteed), while a dedicated VPS handles ZATCA EDI compliance (XML generation, signing, API submission). A bidirectional sync module bridges 18 data models between the two systems with SAVEPOINT transaction protection.

The sync_src_database module was refactored from eval() to json.loads() for security. We added cycle detection for circular FK relationships, thread safety locks for concurrent operations, and batch processing to prevent timeout errors on large invoice payloads.

UBL 2.1 XML invoice generation, X.509 certificate management, SHA-256 hash computation, QR code embedding (seller, VAT, totals, hash), and REST API integration with the government portal. All validated against ZATCA's sandbox before production deployment.

div.h2: Building Agriculture ERP with Odoo: Farm Management for Qatf Company
div.p: Agricultural operations have unique requirements that standard ERP modules don't address. We built a comprehensive farm_management addon for Odoo 17 that handles hierarchical farm locations, crop management, and harvest tracking.

The farms.locations model supports 4 levels: Farm → Sector → Unite → House. Each level links to analytic accounts for cost tracking. Workers are assigned per location with payroll integration. Kanban views enable drag-and-drop farm management.

Work orders are modeled after mrp.production but adapted for farming operations (planting, irrigation, fertilizing, harvesting). Each work order links to specific farm locations and crops, tracks labor hours, material usage, and produces inventory movements.

The crop.crop model manages varieties, planting dates, expected yields, and actual harvests. Stock movement wizards automatically create warehouse receipts when harvests are recorded. Analytics dashboards show yield per location, cost per crop, and seasonal comparisons.

div.h2: Hospital IT Infrastructure: Furkan Surgical Center Case Study
div.p: Deploying complete IT infrastructure for a surgical center requires careful planning across networking, surveillance, servers, and software. Here's what we delivered for Furkan Surgical Center in Aswan.

Structured Cat6 cabling across 3 floors. VLANs per department (surgery, pharmacy, admin, guest). Dedicated server room with rack-mount servers, UPS, and environmental monitoring. Redundant internet links (fiber + 4G failover) for 99.9% uptime.

IP cameras in operating rooms (2MP dome), corridors (4MP bullet), pharmacy (PTZ), parking (8MP). NVR with RAID5 storage for 30-day retention. Mobile app for remote viewing. Motion detection alerts for restricted areas. Integration with access control system.

Ubuntu 22.04 servers, PostgreSQL 16 database, Nginx reverse proxy, Odoo 17 for hospital management (patients, appointments, pharmacy, billing). Docker containers for isolated services. Proxmox for VM management. Automated daily backups to offsite storage.

div.h2: How to Implement AI Intelligence in Your Odoo POS and Marketing
div.p: Machine learning is no longer just for big tech companies. We've published two production-tested AI modules on the Odoo Apps Store that bring intelligent automation to POS transactions and marketing campaigns.

Instead of cashiers manually suggesting products, our AI analyzes the current cart, customer history, and inventory levels to recommend complementary items in real-time. The system processes recommendations in under 100ms — fast enough that cashiers don't notice the latency. One-click product addition, full Arabic/English support, and graceful degradation if the AI service is unavailable.

Campaign performance prediction using machine learning. The system scores leads, forecasts ROI per campaign, and recommends budget allocation. Built with Clean Architecture (DDD + TDD), the module separates business logic from infrastructure — making it easy to swap ML backends or add new scoring rules.

A retail chain using AI POS Copilot saw average basket size increase by 24%. A marketing agency using AI Marketing Copilot reduced campaign costs by 18% while improving ROI by 35%. Both modules are free to install from the Odoo Apps Store with demo data included.

div.h2: Odoo AI Integration Architecture: Clean Design for Long-Term Maintenance
div.p: Most Odoo AI modules are quick hacks. We built ours using Domain-Driven Design, Clean Architecture, and Test-Driven Development — so they scale with your business.

Domain Layer: Business entities (campaigns, products, customers), value objects, rules. Application Layer: Use cases that orchestrate domain logic. Infrastructure Layer: Database, external APIs, file storage. Controller Layer: HTTP endpoints, Odoo RPC calls. This separation means you can change storage backends or ML providers without touching business logic.

Every module includes comprehensive tests: unit tests for domain rules, integration tests for database interactions, behavior tests for user workflows. Test coverage helps catch regressions early and makes refactoring safe.

We model the business domain explicitly — not just database tables. For AI Marketing Copilot: Campaign, ScoringRule, DecisionLog as domain entities with business constraints. This makes the code intent-clear and testable.
